name: howto
title: Set up a KitchenAid tilt-head the way the manual says
sub: Six steps for the first week, while the return window is open
footer: From KitchenAid's owner's manuals (KSM150, Mini KSM3300 series) and KitchenAid's help pages, read Nov 27, 2026.

items.head: Check the model
items.body: The plate under the head or the box should say K45SS, KSM150, KSM3316 or KSM55, the one you paid for.

items.head: Do the dime test
items.body: Dime in the empty steel bowl, flat beater, speed 1. It should nudge the dime, not drag it.

items.head: Turn the screw a little
items.body: Clockwise lowers the beater on a tilt-head. At most 1/8 to 1/4 turn at a time.

items.head: Dough on speed 2
items.body: The manual: never above speed 2 for yeast dough. About 2 minutes after it clings to the hook.

items.head: Respect the flour limit
items.body: Stiff dough is what makes tilt-heads bounce and run hot. Split big batches.

items.head: Let it cool
items.body: If it stops or feels hot, unplug it and wait about 30 minutes before the next batch.
